summary: @vaultflow/update-flow is a decoy wrapper that loads sibling @vaultflow/create-flow on require
details: The package's index.js is a verbatim copy of the well-known feross/buffer module with a single injected top-level statement: `var ins = import('@vaultflow/create-flow"');`, executed as soon as the module is required. `@vaultflow/create-flow` is declared as a runtime dependency and therefore installed alongside this package; requiring @vaultflow/update-flow causes that sibling to be loaded and executed in the consumer's process. Package metadata is fraudulent and inconsistent across every field: name is @vaultflow/update-flow, homepage/bugs point at github.com/guilderguzman/sql-link (unrelated), keywords are 'node'/'sql', and the README describes 'bare-stream' / '@sql-access/nods' — none of which match the buffer code actually shipped. The wrapper-plus-sibling shape is a loader stub whose only functional contribution over stock buffer is pulling @vaultflow/create-flow into the installer's runtime, with the real payload hosted in that sibling package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
